recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中散在數顆大型組織球（箭頭），細胞質大量淡藍灰色、呈細小空泡的泡沫狀／肥皂泡樣（soap bubble），核小而偏位；插圖放大可見細緻多空泡的細胞質，提示儲積症，本例為 Niemann-Pick 病 C 型。
features: Large histiocytes (arrowheads) several times the size of surrounding myeloid cells, scattered singly
Abundant pale gray-blue cytoplasm filled with innumerable small uniform vacuoles giving a foamy/soap-bubble appearance
Small, round, eccentric nuclei with condensed chromatin
Inset: high-power view showing finely vacuolated cytoplasm with occasional larger clear vacuoles, lacking the fibrillary crumpled-tissue-paper texture of Gaucher cells
Background of cellular trilineage marrow with erythroid and myeloid precursors and platelet clumps
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a cellular background of maturing hematopoietic elements with several scattered large histiocytes. These cells have abundant pale gray-blue cytoplasm distended by numerous small, uniform vacuoles imparting a foamy, soap-bubble appearance, and small eccentric nuclei. The high-power inset confirms finely vacuolated rather than fibrillary cytoplasm. Findings are consistent with foamy storage histiocytes, suggestive of a lipid storage disorder such as Niemann-Pick disease; enzymatic assay (acid sphingomyelinase), oxysterol/biomarker studies, and NPC1/NPC2 sequencing are required for classification.

ddx.vs: Gaucher cells have fibrillary, striated 'wrinkled tissue paper' cytoplasm rather than discrete small vacuoles, and show low glucocerebrosidase activity.
Sea-blue histiocytes contain blue-green ceroid granules on Romanowsky stain rather than clear foamy vacuoles, though they can coexist in Niemann-Pick disease.
Morphology of foamy cells is similar; ASM deficiency shows markedly low sphingomyelinase activity and SMPD1 mutations, whereas type C has normal to borderline enzyme and NPC1/NPC2 mutations.

ddx.dx: Reactive lipid-laden macrophages (e.g., hyperlipidemia, TPN, infection)
ddx.vs: Reactive foamy macrophages are fewer and accompany the clinical context, and lack genetic or enzymatic evidence of storage disease.
